chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Mutawakkil narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from al-Abbas ibn Amr al-Faqimi, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, that a man asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

about Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He: Does He have satisfaction and anger? He said: Yes, and that is not like what is found in creatures. This is because satisfaction and anger are intrusions that enter into him, transferring him from one state to another; they are active, composite, with things having an entry into him. But our Creator has no entry for things into Him; He is One, One in Essence, One in Meaning. So His satisfaction is His reward and His anger is His punishment, without anything interlacing Him to agitate Him and transfer Him from one state to another, for that is indeed the characteristic of the created, the incapable and the needy. Whereas He, Blessed and Exalted, is the Strong, the Mighty. He has no need for anything from what He created, and all His creation is needy of Him. He created things not out of need nor cause, by invention and innovation.
ai.seo_question: How is Allah's satisfaction and anger different from human emotions?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* articulates the Shia doctrine of divine simplicity by distinguishing Allah's attributes from human emotions, which are viewed as accidental changes (*taghayyur*) caused by external stimuli. It emphasizes that divine satisfaction and wrath are inherent to His essence and do not involve agitation or need, thereby refuting anthropomorphism and affirming His absolute self-sufficiency (*Al-Ghani*) compared to the contingent nature of creation.
